analysis: Examined the two head_text units of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 3999-4490), which are a documentation-only change. The file_changes patch shows a date bump, a new paragraph at 3528-3536 on the cluster service heartbeat (DARKBLOOM_CLUSTER_MEMBER_HEALTH_FILE, service-health.json vs part-health.json), and a rewrite at 5230-5235 on cluster runtime facts (a signed release computes and registers cluster_runtime digests). The supplied units fall in the unchanged TP/GLM/KV/SSD prefix-record text, so they carry no new behavior. I checked them against the threat model, including the T-041 prefix-cache and SSD at-rest tier and TB-002/TB-007. The unchanged text still describes sealed (AES-GCM) all-sums, a load agreement that fails closed on mismatched precision or policy, and SSD records bound to partition, tenant scope and encoding, with refusal and deletion of foreign records. These are consistent with the T-041 posture and none is weakened. The SSD text (documented in the unchanged docs) keeps the KEK-rooted, HMAC-named, encrypted design. It adds a lossy-by-contract quantized record encoding (default balanced) for cluster prefixes; the `native` option keeps byte-exact records. This concerns accuracy, not confidentiality, and the surrounding text is not part of this PR's diff. Remaining integration questions: the patch excerpt is truncated, and the 3528-3536 and 5230-5235 hunks sit outside the supplied numbered units. The claimed health-file separation and the release-computed cluster_runtime approval digests are code behaviors not visible here. A reviewer should check that the part health path cannot be steered by an environment-supplied key to overwrite or spoof the supervisor liveness file. A reviewer should also check that a release-registered approval digest is derived only from the signed final app, as the new text states. No concrete regression is identifiable from the supplied evidence.
